title: Flat Swap in Berlin - Quick Summary
kicker: WALK OF BERLIN • LIVING IN BERLIN
items: **Who owns the two flats decides the rent.** The seven state-owned companies (degewo, GESOBAU, Gewobag, HOWOGE, STADT UND LAND, WBM, berlinovo) own about **370,000 flats**; everything else counts as private for a swap.

**On the state-owned swap portal both net cold rents stay unchanged.** It runs on inberlinwohnen.de since 2018 and matches tenants across all seven companies; you need to be the main tenant with a lease that is not terminated.
**It is slow:** in 2024 the swap route produced **327 new leases** across the whole state-owned stock, so keep the search wide and running for months.

**Shrinking? Use the downsizing offer.** Since **1 September 2025** your state-owned company makes up to three offers within twelve months for a flat at least one room and 10 m² smaller, at the local comparative rent without a new-letting surcharge.

**A private swap is a new lease.** There is no right to swap, both landlords must agree, and the rent cap allows up to **10 percent above the comparative rent**, or the previous tenant's rent if that was higher.
**My move:** read your lease for the landlord and the rent per m², register on the portal if you are state-owned, and get any private landlord's new rent in writing before anyone gives notice.
